chunks: 1934 - 'Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr Layth al-Murādī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: 'When does food become forbidden for the fasting person, and when does the salat, the salat of al-fajr, become permissible?' So he said to me: 'When the dawn stretches across, and it is like a white cloth, then food becomes forbidden for the fasting person, and the salat, the salat of al-fajr, becomes permissible.'
I said: 'Are we not still within the time until the rays of the sun rise?' He said: 'Far from it! Where are you being taken by that? That is the prayer of children.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer, here specifically the dawn prayer
key_terms.الطَّعَامُ: food, whose consumption becomes forbidden at true dawn for the fasting person
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: the dawn, specifically the true dawn spreading across the horizon
key_terms.الْقُبْطِيَّةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ: a white cloth, used here as a simile for the appearance of dawn
key_terms.شُعَاعُ الشَّمْسِ: the rays of the sun, mentioned as a point after which one should not delay the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الصِّبْيَانِ: the prayer of children, meaning an immature or incorrect timing of prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer whose time begins at true dawn

ai.seo_question: When does eating become forbidden for the fasting person, and when does the time of salat al-fajr begin?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the beginning of true dawn marks both the prohibition of eating for the fasting person and the permissibility of the salat of al-fajr. It rejects delaying the prayer until sunrise light becomes apparent, describing that as the prayer of children.
